title: Vision Transformers versus convolutional neural networks for fine-grained orchid genus identification in a species-rich, data-poor flora: a controlled benchmark on the Orchidaceae of New Guinea
abstract: arXiv:2609.24064v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: New Guinea is the world's richest island flora (~2,856 orchid species), yet most species are represented by only a handful of photographs, far fewer than direct species-level classification requires. Methods for fine-grained identification in such species-rich, data-poor floras are needed, and it remains unclear which backbone architecture and pretraining strategy best support them. We built a two-stage system that first predicts the genus of a query photograph, then retrieves visually similar reference images of candidate species using FAISS. We compared four pretrained backbones -- two Vision Transformers (ViTs; DINOv2, BioCLIP 2) and two CNNs (ConvNeXt V2-L, EfficientNetV2-L) -- fine-tuned under an identical protocol on a fixed, species-stratified partition of 16,701 photographs spanning 120 genera and 1,350 species, assessing accuracy, calibration, error structure, species retrieval, and open-set detection of novel genera. translated_abstract: 新几内亚拥有世界上最丰富的岛屿植物区系（约2,856种兰花），然而大多数物种仅有少量照片，远低于直接进行物种级分类所需的数据量。针对此类物种丰富、数据匮乏的植物区系，亟需细粒度识别方法，但目前尚不清楚哪种骨干网络架构和预训练策略最能支持这类方法。我们构建了一个两阶段系统：首先预测查询照片所属的属，然后使用FAISS检索候选物种的视觉相似参考图像。我们在完全相同的微调协议下，比较了四种预训练骨干网络——两种视觉Transformer（ViT；DINOv2、BioCLIP 2）和两种卷积神经网络（ConvNeXt V2-L、EfficientNetV2-L）——实验基于涵盖120个属、1,350个物种的16,701张照片的固定物种分层划分数据集，从准确率、校准度、错误结构、物种检索以及新属开集检测等多个维度进行了评估。DINOv2在……
tldr: 该研究针对新几内亚物种丰富但数据匮乏的兰科植物，构建了“属级预测+FAISS相似图像检索”的两阶段细粒度识别系统，并在统一协议下受控比较了视觉Transformer（DINOv2、BioCLIP 2）与卷积神经网络（ConvNeXt V2-L、EfficientNetV2-L）四种预训练骨干在准确率、校准、检索和开集检测上的表现。
en_tdlr: This study establishes a two-stage fine-grained identification system (genus prediction plus FAISS similar-image retrieval) for New Guinea's species-rich, data-poor orchid flora, and provides a controlled benchmark comparing Vision Transformers (DINOv2, BioCLIP 2) against CNNs (ConvNeXt V2-L, EfficientNetV2-L) across accuracy, calibration, retrieval, and open-set detection.
